name: Phaseglass Quantum
title: Two-Copy Symmetry-Sector Discrimination Beyond Matched Block Purities
summary: A two-copy quantum measurement distinguishes states whose whole-block purity statistics are identical.
finding: On the specified eight-qubit problem, exact success is 75%, above a certified 66.91% upper bound for separate-copy measurements. At eight copies, simulated accuracy is 97.075% versus 81.600% for a model-aware reference.
scope: The exact theorem uses two total copies and specified symmetry-preserving state families. Longer-budget comparisons are empirical. No hardware, asymptotic, or general phase-recognition advantage is established.

name: Quantum Records
title: Opposite Encoding Preferences for Quantum-Record Consensus and Pooled Inference
summary: The best encoding for separated observers can be the worse encoding when their records are read together.
finding: The study solves a prescribed pure-product encoder problem under a common random-rotation channel. At an exact benchmark, the optimized consensus gap is 1/16; a coherent-state realization also has rational bounds for unrestricted local measurements.
scope: The result holds within explicit encoder and noise assumptions. Generic ordering reversal already occurs classically. Historical priority, an entanglement advantage, and experimental validation are not established.
versionNote: The selected rebuild of the One-Shot Quantum Darwinism project. It supersedes the earlier allocation and analytic-transition drafts.

name: Neutrino Moments
title: Exact Frequency Uncertainty from Neutrino Angular Moments
summary: Exact certificates describe which growing frequencies limited angular-moment information permits.
finding: Positive moment completions yield exact frequency-compatibility tests and sharp growth bounds in specified axial and nonaxial models. The published counter-flux test rejects none of the reproduced closure modes, leaving practical usefulness unresolved.
scope: These are information bounds for restricted local, collisionless fast-flavor models, rather than predictions for a supernova. Some later extensions await independent review; scientific priority remains unconfirmed.

name: Manifold
title: Moment-Weighted Fourier Envelopes for Heat Actions: A Reproducible Algorithm-Discovery Study
summary: A spectral-moment stopping rule is tested against established methods for sparse diffusion calculations.
finding: The original rule saves 0–8.71% of matrix-vector products and misses both frozen practical targets. A separate engineering continuation runs 4.46–8.01 times faster than unchanged v1, primarily through checker improvements.
scope: The numerical-baseline comparisons remain mixed. The core identities have established precedents, application novelty is unresolved, and no complete floating-point certificate or algorithmic breakthrough is claimed.
metricLabel: reference-checked timed outputs across both studies

name: InertiaForge
title: inertiaforge: Auditing Contact Dynamics and the Limits of Gradient Agreement
summary: A rigid-body engine tests whether agreement across simulation refinements makes a contact derivative trustworthy.
finding: The proposed gate accepts 18 of 19 smooth held-out derivatives, but only three accepted derivatives meet the accuracy target. A restricted, established event-time baseline passes all 19 supported smooth cases.
scope: The study rejects the proposed reliability hypothesis. Its separate 5.474 mm measured-trajectory transfer result covers three bouncing-ball trials; it does not validate general contact physics or certify gradients.

name: Cragshift
title: cragshift: Quality-aware Camera–Laser Monitoring with an Auditable Simulated Rock-slope Benchmark
summary: Learned sensor-quality weighting is evaluated on original camera–laser surveys of procedural rock slopes.
finding: On sixteen fresh simulated sites, recall is 82.33% versus 75.93% for simple fusion, at unchanged observation coverage. The paired site-bootstrap recall gain is 6.39 percentage points, with interval [4.28, 8.86].
scope: False-positive rates are 5.60% and 5.42%; false-alarm equality is not established. This is a preserved simulation study. A later realism and false-positive revision was still unfinished at this snapshot; no field-safety or collapse-prediction claim is supported.
metricLabel: recall gain on fresh simulated sites

name: TAILSENTRY
title: TAILSENTRY: Structure-Certified Conditional Union Sampling for Rare Losses
summary: An auditable rare-event sampler tests probability bounds, missed catastrophic modes, and efficiency.
finding: Across 17,280 complete algorithm runs, the selected candidate loses to conditional scrambled Sobol on the primary efficiency comparison. A missing-mode test also shows ordinary intervals can be badly overconfident despite large observed effective sample sizes.
scope: The numerical results concern supported Gaussian and Student-t loss models. Conditioning improves the corresponding raw union sampler, but neither an original general estimator nor superiority to the strongest comparator is established.

name: RevertLab
title: RevertLab: Cost-aware Continuation under Rival Spread Dynamics
summary: A chronological pairs-trading study values convergence, relationship failure, both trading legs, and costs.
finding: The proposed rule loses 1.20% on deposited capital during the reserved 2023–2025 evaluation. Its uncertainty interval against the development-selected gate includes harm, and simpler methods perform better.
scope: The study uses six crypto assets and three candidate pairs with simulated borrowing and execution. It establishes no economic advantage or historical short availability. The retained two-leg account supports independent reconciliation.

name: Counterglass
title: Counterglass: Stateful Counterfactual Failure Evidence and a Budgeted Search Study
summary: Checkpointed tool-agent executions expose failures that successful responses can conceal.
finding: A locked 1,280-episode study tests ten search policies. The proposed pooled selector misses its frozen improvement target and loses to a simpler schema heuristic. All 7,177 unique recorded pairs were freshly replayed and independently checked with zero mismatches.
scope: The evaluation uses three authored workflow structures. Separate ToolSandbox and local-model cases support execution evidence, not broad selector generalization. Evidence records are unsigned and do not prove arbitrary agent behavior.

name: Spectral Ambiguity
title: Projected Witness Reuse for Positive Spectral Experiment Design
summary: Cached adversarial spectra accelerate a measurement-selection calculation, while acquisition tests fail their scientific target.
finding: The original finite-menu study reports a 5.16× median selection speedup over warm-started HiGHS. Physical acquisition reaches the target in 4/9 cases versus 6/9 for conventional design. A corrected follow-up finds all five policies miss the target in all nine new cases.
scope: The speedup is for a specialized computation, rather than demonstrated scientific acquisition superiority. The follow-up identifies a resolution bottleneck and leaves independent physical sampling costs unestablished. The original and corrective reports remain separate.

supplements.title: Corrective follow-up: A Consistent Cell Model Does Not Establish Spectral Acquisition Superiority

name: FUSIONZERO
title: Current Conservation Does Not Ensure Accurate Equilibrium Geometry
summary: Tokamak reconstruction studies separate numerical current constraints from useful predictions of equilibrium geometry.
finding: All 256 current-constrained predictions pass the declared feasibility and optimality checks, but the local reconstruction score is 0.783302 versus 0.869123 for direct flux regression. Two earlier notes retain flux-relabeling failures and a controlled passive-current ambiguity study.
scope: This is a development snapshot of ongoing research. No original inverse algorithm, blind-test improvement, experimental ambiguity, or cross-machine performance is established.

supplements.title: Supplement: Passive-Current Ambiguity in Nonmagnetic Equilibrium Reconstruction

name: COUNTERPATCH
title: COUNTERPATCH: Exact Data-Repair Counterfactuals and a Negative Result for Added Search
summary: Finite training-data repairs are measured through exact ridge counterfactuals and conventional retraining.
finding: The preserved report’s selector ties greedy on digits and gains 1.4% on Airfoil, with a paired interval crossing zero. A conventional full-data influence baseline recovers more mean error in the primary corrupted settings.
scope: The report concerns fixed-feature ridge pipelines and controlled defects. Exact update identities are established methods. Later research continued without a successful new mechanism; this is the completed October report, not a claim that the broader goal succeeded.
